question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2y}{(x+1)^{2}}, & x\ge 0,\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the expected value of $Y.$
question.worked_solution:
The marginal density function for $Y$ when $0\le y\le 1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{2y}{(x+1)^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2y{lim}_{b\to \infty }{\int }_{0}^{b}\frac{1}{(x+1)^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2y{lim}_{b\to \infty }{[-\frac{1}{(x+1)}]}_{0}^{b} \\  & =2y{lim}_{b\to \infty }(1-\frac{1}{b+1}) \\  & =2y.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is given by

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}2y, & 0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the  expected value of $Y$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }y\cdot {f}_{Y}(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y\cdot 2y\,\text{d}y \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =2{[\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =2(\frac{1}{3}-0) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
